latest.title: Phase separation in cell-extracellular matrix adhesion: looking back and moving forward.
latest.summary: The exponential growth of phase separation research has uncovered fundamental concepts across biology, making it timely to reassess findings across fields. Here, we summarise advances linking biomolecular condensation to integrin-mediated cell-extracellular matrix adhesion and migration. latest.title: A Multimodal Knowledge Tree Construction Model for Tomato Phenological Knowledge
latest.summary: Fragmented agricultural multimedia resources hinder explicit hierarchical organization of crop phenological knowledge. This study formulates tomato phenological knowledge organization as supervised parent placement within a fixed BBCH hierarchy. The framework combines directional multimodal scoring with constrained decoding to link image observations to traceable developmental paths. A frozen Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B encoder mapped textual concepts and plant images into a shared 2048-dimensional space. Modality-specific projections, availability masks, and gated fusion produced unified representations, which were mapped into a 128-dimensional Poincaré ball for directional parent–child…

latest.title: Development of a manganese-enriched fungal biomaterial and its effect on coral photosynthesis.
latest.summary: Biomaterials made with mycelium, the vegetative part of fungi, offer an innovative method for delivering micronutrients for bioremediation in aquatic environments. Manganese is a crucial trace element for corals and their symbionts, supporting both photosynthesis and antioxidant defenses. items.title: When measurements of AI systems disagree A methodological review of dissociations in AI safety
items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence safety research compares systems' answers and actions with output probabilities, generated reasoning, internal activations and monitoring judgments. These measurements can disagree about what a system knows, what influenced its response and whether unwanted behavior occurred. This critical tutorial review organizes the emerging literature around five comparisons: relative sensitivity, incremental value, functional dissociation, causal intervention and targeted robustness. Worked examples distinguish reported findings, their inferential limits and informative follow-up comparisons. The comparisons are introduced through simpler settings and then applied…

items.title: The Impact of Hurricane Helene on the Incidence of Acute Gastrointestinal Illness in North Carolina, US: A Controlled Interrupted Time Series Analysis
items.summary: In September 2024, Hurricane Helene caused significant flooding in western North Carolina (NC), leading to concerns surrounding water quality, including the risk of acute gastrointestinal illness (AGI). The potential for flooding-related drinking water contamination is exacerbated for private well users, who comprised a large proportion of the population most affected by the hurricane. Here we investigated the impact of Hurricane Helene on AGI and determined if this impact was different in areas with greater proportions of residents using private wells. We used electronic health records from Truveta to identify inpatient and outpatient visits to hospitals for AGI in NC from 2016-2024 at…

items.title: A report-supervised EEG-language foundation model enables broad, interactive clinical interpretation
items.summary: Medical AI for complex signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) relies on costly expert annotations and predefined diagnostic labels that fail to capture the richness and nuance of clinical interpretation. Whether models trained on routine clinical reports can overcome these limitations while matching expert-supervised performance remains unclear. We introduce EEG Copilot, a biosignal-language foundation model trained on routine EEG-report pairs without dedicated task-specific expert annotations. Across two external datasets (6,078 EEGs), EEG Copilot performed on par with a state-of-the-art expert-supervised model across 11 shared findings (mean AUROC 0.80-0.81), corroborated by direct…

items.title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
items.summary: Transformer-based foundation models have shown strong potential for modeling longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), yet existing models focus primarily on risk prediction rather than treatment effect estimation, which limits evidence generation. Here, we introduce the ITE-Transformer, a transformer-based framework that combines self-supervised representation learning from longitudinal patient trajectories with doubly robust causal machine learning for predicting individualized treatment effects (ITEs). As a result, our ITE-Transformer allows to study counterfactual questions of how an individual patient's outcome may differ under alternative treatment strategies. The…

items.title: Retinal foundation-model versus ImageNet pretraining for deep learning grading of diabetic retinopathy: an external validation study
items.summary: Abstract Purpose To determine whether retinal foundation-model pretraining reduces the loss of diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading agreement on external fundus-photograph datasets compared with ImageNet-pretrained convolutional networks. Methods RETFound (linear probe and full fine-tuning), EfficientNet-B3 and ResNet-50 were developed on APTOS 2019 (3,662 images) and tested unchanged on Messidor-2 (1,744 images, adjudicated grades) and IDRiD (516 images). The prespecified primary outcome was the difference in internal-to-external quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) drop relative to EfficientNet-B3 for one training run per model; a post hoc analysis averaged three or four runs per model. items.title: MammoInsight: A Unified Multi-Task Deep Learning Framework for Mammography Analysis
items.summary: Abstract Background Mammography interpretation requires simultaneous assessment of multiple clinical attributes such as cancer status, breast density, BI-RADS score, abnormality type, and molecular subtype. The existing AI systems generally address these tasks in isolation, limiting clinical utility and generalizability. Methods We present MammoInsight, a unified multi-task deep learning framework built on MedImageInsight foundation model backbone, incorporating SAM-Med2D-guided region-of-interest pooling, cross-view attention fusion across both standard mammography views, weighted ordinal regression for ordered clinical labels, DHN-NCE contrastive regularisation, and homoscedastic…

items.title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation.
items.summary: AI models remain largely static, yet cancer care never stands still. Evolution of scanning technology, imaging protocols, staging criteria, therapies, and patient populations can silently erode model performance and patient safety. Continual learning (CL) enables models to continuously acquire new knowledge, while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. Here, we review CL methods and their oncology applications, predominantly in imaging and pathology, and discuss CL as an option for maintaining foundation models, alongside recalibration and retraining. We examine translational barriers, including hidden regressions in underrepresented populations, label and concept drift, privacy constraints…

items.title: Bacterial Hsp90 and its interacting partners.
items.summary: Protein quality control depends on molecular chaperones to promote protein folding, remodeling, disaggregation, and degradation. The major families of chaperones present in nearly all organisms are Hsp90, Hsp70, Hsp60, and Clp/Hsp100. Here, we review Hsp90 chaperones with particular emphasis on bacterial Hsp90s. Unlike eukaryotic Hsp90, the bacterial Hsp90 is independent of Hsp90 cochaperones and thus provides a simpler and more accessible system to study the mechanism of action of Hsp90. Despite this simplicity, bacterial Hsp90s are highly homologous to eukaryotic family members and exhibit sensitivity to the same small-molecule inhibitors as eukaryotic Hsp90. Thus, insights gained from…

items.title: Stability and tethering of the preconoidal rings in Toxoplasma gondii.
items.summary: Apicomplexan parasites rely on a specialized apical cytoskeleton to generate the forces required for motility and host-cell invasion. At its core lies the conoid, composed of spiraling tubulin fibers capped by three preconoidal rings (PCRs), which anchor the actin nucleator Formin 1 and contribute to force transmission at the parasite apex. Here, we refine the molecular organization and function of the PCRs in Toxoplasma gondii. We show that PCR composition and stability change during parasite maturation, with a subset of PCR proteins, Pcr2 and Pcr3, adopting a characteristic half-ring organization. We identify MyoL, a divergent pseudomyosin, as a previously unrecognized PCR component.…

items.title: Identification of SAMD4B as a Centrosome-Associated Regulator of the Sonic Hedgehog Signaling Pathway
items.summary: Background: Many protein-protein interactions are required for the assembly and function of primary cilia, microtubule-based organelles critical for the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway and, in turn, for embryonic development and tissue homeostasis. However, our understanding of this complex process remains incomplete. Methods: To identify new regulators of primary cilia formation or function, we carried out proximity labeling experiments and compared interactomes under ciliogenesis-restrictive and permissive conditions. Using an unbiased strategy, we selected candidates that were tested functionally by siRNA-mediated depletion or gene editing, in combination with gene expression…

items.title: A developmental resource mapping tubulin isotype deployment during corneal morphogenesis.
items.summary: Microtubules are core cytoskeletal polymers that support epithelial organization, polarity, and tissue morphogenesis. They are composed of α- and β-tubulin heterodimers encoded by multigene families that generate closely related but distinct isotypes. Although several tubulin isotypes have been implicated in ocular development and disease, their spatial organization during corneal morphogenesis remains poorly defined. Here we establish a resource for visualizing and quantifying tubulin isotype localization during corneal development using the chick embryo. Comparative amino acid sequence analysis demonstrates that chick and human α- and β-tubulin isotypes are highly conserved within…

items.title: Drosophila Orb2 contributes to neural stem cell centrosome asymmetry and cell growth.
items.summary: The deregulation of neural stem cell (NSC) homeostasis underlies neurodevelopmental disorders and tumorigenesis. In the Drosophila larval brain, NSCs divide asymmetrically along an invariant apical-basal axis to yield a larger self-renewing stem cell and a smaller, differentiating sibling. NSC divisions are instructed by centrosomes, which recruit pericentriolar material (PCM) important for microtubule-organizing activity. During interphase, NSC centrosomes are defined by asymmetries in PCM composition and functional activity. These asymmetries help align the mitotic spindle and position the cleavage furrow. Here, we show that the conserved RNA-binding protein Orb2 is required to enrich…

items.title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory.
items.summary: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency…

items.title: Monolayer h-BN RF Switch Toward Monolithic Inductor Switching in Wide-Tuning-Range LC-VCOs.
items.summary: Next-generation wireless systems demand monolithic three-dimensional (3D) system-on-chip architectures to overcome planar scaling limits and reduce interconnect delays. Realizing this back-end-of-line (BEOL) integration on complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) platforms requires ultracompact, high-performance radio-frequency (RF) switches. Here, we present a non-volatile RF switch based on a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) memristor employing an Ag/h-BN/Ag structure. The device exhibits a low SET voltage of 1.11 V and stable endurance exceeding 500 cycles. At 20 GHz, it achieves an insertion loss of 0.81 dB and an isolation of 32.91 dB, enabled by a low on-resistance (R…

items.title: Growth-Spiral Control of Defect Topology and Local Vertical Piezoresponse in Bi4Ti3O12 Thin Films.
items.summary: Aurivillius phase materials are layered ferroelectrics with high thermal stability (>600 °C) and fatigue resistance, yet their polarization is predominantly in-plane, limiting integration into vertical device architectures relevant to future memory, data storage, and neuromorphic computing concepts. Achieving robust vertical polarization in these systems remains fundamentally challenging because of crystallographic symmetry constraints. Although defects can locally reorient polarization, deterministic control of defect topology through growth-mode engineering remains largely unexplored in layered ferroelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that precise control of nominal precursor loading and…

items.title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
items.summary: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM).…

items.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
items.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For…

items.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE)…

items.title: Activity-driven motion and deformation of a circular membrane domain
items.summary: Lipid bilayer membranes are nanometer-thin fluid interfaces characterized by both in-plane fluidity and lateral compositional heterogeneity. Cholesterol-rich liquid domains ("lipid rafts") are thought to regulate the spatial organization of membrane proteins and numerous cellular processes. While the passive diffusion and equilibrium shape fluctuations of membrane domains are well understood, much less is known about how the activity of molecular machines, such as protein pumps and enzymes, influences their mobility and deformation. Here, we analyze the dynamics of a membrane domain driven by an embedded molecular machine within the framework of two-dimensional Stokes flow. The molecular…

items.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
items.summary: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130),…

items.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
items.summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim…

items.title: Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups
items.summary: We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.

items.title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware
items.summary: Frontier text-to-image (T2I) foundation models predominantly rely on multi-billion parameter Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) pretrained across massive compute clusters, creating an accessibility barrier for academic laboratories. When training DiTs from scratch on single consumer GPUs (e.g., an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with 24\,GB VRAM), practitioners encounter three primary bottlenecks: quadratic attention sequence costs, Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation graph breaks induced by variable aspect-ratio bucketing, and an autoencoder throughput wall where frozen Variational Autoencoder (VAE) operations dominate step latency. In this work, we introduce \textbf{Asuka-FM}, an end-to-end system and…

items.title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
items.summary: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible…

items.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
items.summary: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training…

items.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
items.summary: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar…

items.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
items.summary: Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. However, most pathology foundation models are trained on tissue patches and capture cellular features only implicitly, while existing cell-level models are either restricted to specific cell populations or rely on computationally expensive architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters. Applying ViTs directly to small cellular crops also presents an architectural challenge: upsampling increases computational cost without adding morphological information and may introduce interpolation artefacts. To address…

items.title: Exposure-Aware Informative Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the finite-budget exposure-aware informative path planning (IPP) problem for a fleet of mobile sensing agents. The agents map an unknown scalar field while limiting exposure to high field intensity. Existing IPP methods optimize informativeness under motion or resource constraints, but do not address field exposure constraints. We formulate exposure-aware IPP (EA-IPP) as a scalarized bi-objective belief-state Markov decision process that trades the normalized Gaussian-process (GP) information gain against a normalized measurement-derived fleet exposure index. A parameter-shared proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework with decentralized actors and a centralized…

items.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
items.summary: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first…

items.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
items.summary: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser…

items.title: Two powers, one scalar field: unified early and late dark energy
items.summary: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. We consider a double-power potential in which a steep positive-power term can generate an early peak in the scalar energy-density fraction, while an inverse-power term supports late-time acceleration. This evolution requires the steep term to dominate initially and become subdominant later. We test the model against cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillations, and Pantheon+ supernova data, with the SH0ES host-distance calibration. Relative to flat $Λ$CDM, the data fit improves by $Δχ^2_{\rm data}=-6.90$, or…

items.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
items.summary: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

items.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification
items.summary: Pathology foundation models supply strong representations for whole-slide image classification, yet the confidence attached to their predictions remains hard to trust. Prevailing uncertainty estimators act within a single feature space and thereby overlook the uncertainty that the choice of foundation-model representation itself induces. This work introduces CALIFUSE, a calibration-oriented framework that fuses several pathology foundation models for the specific purpose of uncertainty estimation. Departing from accuracy-driven fusion, CALIFUSE reads representational heterogeneity across encoders as an explicit confidence cue. Slide-level decision consensus is coupled with chunk-level…

items.title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement
items.summary: Post-training recursive self-improvement (RSI) iteratively improves a target capability, operationalized by a fixed anchor benchmark, through repeated intervention, training, and evaluation. Yet most loops use the anchor's aggregate score as their sole observation, so early gains give way to stalled progress and repetitive exploration. When this anchor-only feedback ceases to reveal actionable gaps, a plateau may reflect an exhausted observation rather than an exhausted capability. We introduce adaptive observation (AdaObs), an observation-side mechanism of harness evolution that keeps the anchor objective fixed while adapting the active observation. At a plateau, a controller refines…

items.title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the…

items.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
items.summary: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained. Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture,…

items.title: Double determinants of quaternion matrices in the P-generalized determinant framework with applications
items.summary: Building on the P-generalized determinant over quaternions, we introduce the double determinant of arbitrary square quaternion matrices. We then apply the double determinant to obtain a determinant representation for the inverse of any invertible quaternion matrix, without the Hermitian restriction. Furthermore, we establish Cramer's rule for the unique solutions to the quaternion linear equations Ax=b and xA=b, as well as to the quaternion matrix equations AX=B, XA=B, and AXB=C. As an application, we use the determinant representation of the unique solution to AXB=C to design a color image encryption-decryption scheme. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the encryption algorithm…

items.title: Studying AI Act Mentions: A first look at the impact of the European Union's AI regulation on Hugging Face
items.summary: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) entered into force in August 2024, and its obligations apply in stages. Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models have applied since August 2025, and transparency rules since August 2026. These obligations affect developers who share and deploy models and applications on public platforms such as Hugging Face (HF), the largest platform for distributing AI artifacts. However, little is known about how practitioners respond to the regulation in practice. To address this gap, we conducted an empirical study of explicit references to the AI Act on HF. We collected over five million records, including repository cards,…

items.title: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice
items.summary: Reasoning models provide strong multimodal task understanding but struggle with sub-second control because deliberation increases decision latency. Fast decision models can meet the response window, yet prompting and few-shot examples do not readily provide the fine-grained experience required by a new task. Inspired by coached motor learning, this paper presents System-One Recursive Self-Improvement (System-One RSI), which couples two loops. The high-frequency online inner loop is an Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) cycle: a decision model maps each visual observation and task question to structured judgments, and a decision tree converts them into timed actions without invoking a…

items.title: Sequence-encoded amphiphilicity controls the interfacial tension of biomolecular condensates
items.summary: Biomolecular condensates exhibit surprisingly low surface tensions, despite forming dense, liquid-like phases. We propose that the low surface tension partially originates from the segmental amphiphilicity of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) that results in a surfactant-like behavior. We investigate this mechanism using a minimal coarse-grained IDP model containing only hydrophobic and polar residues, allowing us to systematically vary the polar fraction and, for selected cases, to probe the influence of sequence patterning of polar residues. To control for differences in thermodynamic phase behavior, we determine phase coexistence (binodals) for each sequence and compare systems…

items.title: Does It Depend on the Split? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping
items.summary: Self-supervised foundation models are often said to need fewer labels than supervised training. We test this on a forestry task: classifying 20 tree species classes in 0.2 m aerial images from the TreeSatAI dataset. We compare a frozen DINOv3 model pretrained on 493 million satellite images, with only a linear classifier trained on top, against an ImageNet ResNet-50 that is fine-tuned end to end. On the official split, fine-tuning wins clearly (macro F1 0.764 vs. 0.685). However, 28.8% of the official test patches overlap a training or validation patch, and copying the label of the nearest such patch is correct for 83.6% of them. We therefore build a spatial split that holds out whole 2 km…

items.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
items.summary: Generative models produce many candidate solutions but provide no intrinsic signal by which to rank them. One mitigation is to demand a \emph{verifiable artifact}: a program that can be executed against the available evidence. A common concern is that requiring executable verification incurs costs in both solution quality and computational budget. We measure these two costs on the $120$-task ARC-AGI-2 evaluation set. Demanding a verifiable artifact from an LLM reduced the score from $93$ to $68$ of $120$ tasks ($77\%$ to $57\%$). Of those $25$ tasks, $21$ were reached by no program-producing configuration we ran, at any budget, by sampling or by search; yet for $27$ of the $28$ tasks that…

items.title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) is now a standard tool for forecasting the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) plants, yet published accuracy figures are often hard to compare and harder to trust. Many studies validate with random splits, report no reference forecast, and present feature attributions without saying what they can and cannot show. This paper reviews the main families of ML methods for PV power forecasting and resource assessment, from tree ensembles to deep and foundation models, and sets out a reproducible workflow that combines automated model search with explainable AI. The workflow is then tested on an openly available dataset: a 16.32 kWp plant in Porto, Portugal, forecast one day…

items.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
items.summary: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion…

items.title: AdaptReg: Skip-level FiLM Adapter for Task-Specific Adaptation of a Frozen Registration Foundation Model
items.summary: Longitudinal PSMA-PET/CT registration is a key step in assessing treatment response in prostate cancer, and it requires more than generic alignment accuracy: the deformation must preserve lesion volume, so that measured changes in metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis (TLG) reflect treatment response rather than registration artifacts. We propose AdaptReg, which adapts a frozen registration foundation model to such task-specific requirements through a lightweight trainable adapter branch with identity-preserving initialization. Keeping uniGradICON fully frozen, we apply FiLM-style per-voxel affine modulation ($γ$, $β$) to its decoder skip connections; the modulation is…

items.title: MatVerse: A Foundation Model for Materials Science
items.summary: Materials science involves highly heterogeneous scientific information, including textual knowledge, molecular and crystal structures, experimental characterization data, microscopy images, and structure-property relationships. Developing a general-purpose foundation model capable of understanding and reasoning over these diverse materials representations remains challenging. In this technical report, we introduce MatVerse, a materials foundation model built upon Intern-S2-Preview and further specialized through large-scale materials-domain post-training. We construct a large-scale multimodal training corpus covering materials knowledge, scientific reasoning, quantitative problem solving,…

items.title: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage and Concept Erasure in Shared Foundation-Model Embeddings
items.summary: Medical-image embeddings are increasingly shared in place of raw images for authorized downstream tasks, yet they may reveal sensitive attributes. Standard concept-erasure methods target population-level guardedness. However, we prove that, when binary task and sensitive labels are associated, global and task-conditional linear guardedness cannot both hold while a nonzero linear task signal is preserved, so global erasure must either eliminate that signal or retain task-conditional linear leakage. We further show how global erasure affects linear readers' discrimination between positive and negative samples with different sensitive attributes, deriving an approximate closed-form prediction…

items.title: Cyber-Physical RSI for AI-RAN: A Case Study
items.summary: Learned models for radio access networks (RANs) are often developed using simulation, yet their predictions can shift when exposed to physical propagation conditions, protocol behavior, and equipment implementations. This paper presents a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework for AI-RAN that connects a task-oriented student model, an experiment-planning coach agent, a calibratable virtual environment, and a physical host agent. Physical measurements are organized as evidence for both model adaptation and subsequent experiment planning. We examine an implementation of the physical-feedback pathway using ping-pong handover as a case study. The system completes 12 physical…

items.title: A Multimodal Knowledge Tree Construction Model for Tomato Phenological Knowledge
items.summary: Fragmented agricultural multimedia resources hinder explicit hierarchical organization of crop phenological knowledge. This study formulates tomato phenological knowledge organization as supervised parent placement within a fixed BBCH hierarchy. The framework combines directional multimodal scoring with constrained decoding to link image observations to traceable developmental paths. A frozen Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B encoder mapped textual concepts and plant images into a shared 2048-dimensional space. Modality-specific projections, availability masks, and gated fusion produced unified representations, which were mapped into a 128-dimensional Poincaré ball for directional parent–child…

items.summary: A cross-species ontology and SBGN pathway-map toolkit for quantum-biological processes. Companion software to a review of plant responses to near-null magnetic fields (Porterfield & Barker, in preparation). items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Public Procurement in Small Developing Economies: Perceptions and Readiness of Procurement Officials in Bhutan
items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer unprecedented potential for enhancing sustainable public procurement (SPP) in small developing economies (SDEs), yet empirical research on AI adoption readiness in developing economy public sectors remains sparse. This integrated study: (i) develops a conceptual framework synthesizing Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE), and Responsible AI Governance principles; (ii) presents an AI Procurement Maturity Model (AIPMM) tracing evolution from traditional to intelligent procurement; (iii) provides empirical evidence from 96 Bhutanese procurement officials; and (iv) proposes research propositions…

Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
items.summary: Introduction: Spatial transcriptomics can resolve compartment-specific molecular programs in kidney disease, but its cost and technical requirements limit its use in clinical diagnostics and in large biopsy archives. Predicting spatial gene expression from routine histology with artificial intelligence could extend molecular characterization to existing clinically annotated kidney tissue collections. Methods: We adapted DeepSpot-M, a pretrained multimodal foundation model that predicts spatial gene expression from histology, using paired hematoxylin and eosin images and Visium spatial transcriptomics from 209 Kidney Precision Medicine Project (KPMP) participants. items.title: A high-performance self-rectifying memristor for reliable neuromorphic plasticity and long-distance AM signal modulation/demodulation.
items.summary: As an innovative approach for addressing the parasitic current issue in large-scale integrated circuits, self-rectifying memristors eliminate the need for extra external circuitry, which not only significantly cuts down on manufacturing costs but also paves the way for advancing high-density integration technology. Herein, Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) is innovatively introduced as the resistive switching material, and a synaptic memristor with excellent self-rectifying characteristics is successfully developed. Under electrical regulation, the device features a rectification ratio (RR) up to ∼1.2 × 103, an On/Off ratio of ∼1.7 × 103 at 1.2 V bias voltage, a low set voltage of ∼-0.60 V, and a stable…

items.title: Conductive filament dynamics in memristive sensors: from resistive switching mechanisms to multifunctional sensing applications.
items.summary: With advances in sensor technology, various sensors are being widely applied, becoming an indispensable part of modern life. However, constrained by inherent sensing mechanisms, certain performance limitations remain difficult to improve through conventional modification methods. Herein, we focus on memristors for various sensing applications, summarizing how their resistive switching effect enables the modulation of device performance. First, the development history of memristors is outlined, and recent research progress in the fields of gas sensing, optoelectronic sensing, and pressure sensing is summarized. Meanwhile, representative memristors are employed as examples to investigate the…

items.title: Superconductivity in hyperbolic spaces: Regular hyperbolic lattices and Ginzburg-Landau theory
items.summary: We study s -wave superconductivity in hyperbolic spaces using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes theory for discrete hyperbolic lattices and the Ginzburg-Landau theory for the continuous hyperbolic plane. Hyperbolic lattices maintain a finite fraction of boundary sites regardless of system size, thus fundamentally altering superconductivity through enhanced boundary effects absent in flat space. Within the BCS framework for hyperbolic lattices, uniform systems reproduce standard bulk behavior, whereas finite systems with open boundaries, studied through exact diagonalization and Cayley-tree approximations, exhibit boundary-enhanced superconductivity and boundary-only superconducting states that…

items.title: Curvature estimates for hypersurfaces of constant sum Hessian curvature in Hn+1
items.summary: We study the asymptotic Plateau problem in hyperbolic space for constant sum Hessian curvature. Assuming that n≥2 and α>0, we establish curvature estimates for Γ˜n,α-convex hypersurfaces with σn bounded from below, i.e. σn>−A, A∈((n−1)σ/α,+∞), and a prescribed asymptotic boundary at the infinity for constant Sn,α curvature.

items.title: LoopROS: A Deployable Embodied Recursive Self-Improvement Framework Based on Logical and Physical Constraints
items.summary: Embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) endows robots with the capacity to progressively refine manipulation skills through real-world physical interaction, representing a cornerstone toward generalpurpose embodied intelligence. Yet existing embodied RSI frameworks largely remain simulationbound: they fail to realize closed-loop RSI when transferred onto uncalibrated real-world robots. This paper presents LoopROS, a deployable RSI framework built upon a constraints-as-policy principle for embodied robot. With In-Context Learning-Based Logical Constraints, the LoopROS parses real-world demonstrations, to guide segment selection, outcome assessment, and experience reuse. With Segmentwise…

items.title: From Recursive Self-Improvement to Human-AI Reciprocal Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement advances most readily in domains where results can be verified reliably, such as mathematics and coding. Beyond these domains, progress slows as reliable signals for evaluating and guiding improvement become harder to obtain, resulting in a jagged frontier of AI capabilities. Yet even where AI self-improves autonomously, its growing capabilities do not necessarily translate into greater human ability to understand, use and build upon its outputs, challenging both continued human participation and effective oversight. We argue that recursive progress should therefore also encompass the growth of human capabilities. We propose Recursive Reciprocal Improvement (RRI)…

items.title: Multiobjective exploration of intramolecular torsional space.
items.summary: We present an exploration-first strategy for intramolecular conformational search. Because practical quantum-chemical (QC) models are approximate, candidate retention combines energy and interaction descriptors as separate objectives, while structural diversity is preserved until post-search reduction. The SEEKER (Structural Ensemble Exploration through Knowledge-Guided Evaluation and Routing) program explores explicitly declared acyclic torsions through unit-quaternion rotations while retaining fixed ring families. We assess reference-set coverage for amino acids, the sugars D-glucose, erythrulose, and fructose, and thiopronine using per-reference nearest-candidate heavy-atom…

items.title: A Survey on Recursive Self-Improvement in Healthcare AI Agents
items.summary: Advances in persistent memory, reusable skills and adaptive training are making recursive self-improvement (RSI) increasingly relevant to healthcare agents. RSI concerns changes to the procedures that generate future improvements. This survey connects these developments with healthcare evidence by distinguishing component updates, training-generator changes and revisions of improvement procedures. We examine applications in diagnosis, reporting and question answering, together with challenges in evaluation, reliability, privacy and update governance. Current evidence supports persistent component updates and selected generator gains, while the effects of revised improvement procedures on…

items.title: Hyperbolic neural networks for biologically informed classification of white blood cells and hematopoietic cell states in peripheral blood smears
items.summary: Abstract Automated white blood cell (WBC) classification in peripheral blood smears supports morphological assessment of hematological disorders, but most deep learning classifiers treat cell categories as independent labels and do not account for hematopoietic maturation. We propose a hyperbolic classification framework that combines a ResNet-18 feature extractor with a prototype-based classifier in the Poincaré ball, allowing biologically related cell states to be represented in a geometry suited to hierarchical structure. The model was evaluated on a curated dataset of 129,174 annotated single-cell images mapped to 14 blood cell classes, including leukocyte subtypes, hematopoietic…

items.title: LoopROS: A Dual Recursive Self-Improvement Loops of Robotic Operating System Based on Functional Constraints and Trajectory Tuning
items.summary: Recent advances in foundation models have enabled robotic agents to reason, plan, and adapt their actions through physical interaction. Yet successful execution does not necessarily translate into lasting improvement across tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising paradigm for robotic agents to continuously refine their capabilities through experience, but requires preserving functional knowledge, adapting execution to changing physical conditions, and retaining reusable corrections. We introduce LoopROS, a dual-loop robotic agent framework that couples functionally constrained execution with experience-driven improvement. Within each episode, functional constraint-guided…

items.title: SEA-Lab: Experiment-grounded recursive self-improvement in an automated laboratory
items.summary: AI scientists can generate hypotheses, plans, and protocols. Translating these outputs into reliable experiments requires adapting them to local equipment and resources using feedback from observed outcomes. A key challenge is to retain laboratory execution feedback as reusable knowledge for subsequent planning. We present SEA-Lab ( S elf- E volving A utonomous Lab), which combines an environment-grounded Dry-Lab Harness that generates protocols and machine-readable procedures, a wet-lab execution harness that coordinates heterogeneous devices and records execution traces and experimental measurements, and a recursive self-improvement mechanism that uses physical feedback to revise…

items.title: NeuroMASS v4: Geometry-Aware Neural Population Dynamics via Learnable Hyperbolic Latent Representations and Biologically-Calibrated Diagonal State Space Models
items.summary: The geometry of neural population activity is a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. We present NeuroMASS v4, a novel architecture that introduces learnable hyperbolic latent geometry to spike-train co-smoothing on the Neural Latents Benchmark (NLB’21). Our central scientific claim is that the curvature c of a Poincaré-ball—learned end-to-end from extracellular spike recordings— constitutes a biologically interpretable geometric signature: significantly positive for ring-manifold motor circuits (MC_Maze, MC_RTT) and near-zero for topologically unstructured frontal circuits (DMFC_RSG). items.title: Development of a manganese-enriched fungal biomaterial and its effect on coral photosynthesis.
items.summary: Biomaterials made with mycelium, the vegetative part of fungi, offer an innovative method for delivering micronutrients for bioremediation in aquatic environments. Coral reefs are highly productive marine ecosystems; however, their resilience has been threatened by anthropogenic climate change. Manganese is a crucial trace element for corals and their symbionts, supporting both photosynthesis and antioxidant defenses. In this study, we developed and characterized a fungal biomaterial (FG) and its manganese-loaded derivative (FGMn) using spectroscopic and thermal techniques, with the aim of creating devices capable of releasing Mn to corals in a controlled manner. items.title: From quantum brain to quantum mind: The ontological promotion gap in quantum-biological theories of consciousness.
items.summary: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. items.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
items.summary: Motivation Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline. Results BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. items.title: Rotor-Twisted Clifford–Mandelbrot Sets: Breaking the Planar Reduction with Geometric Algebra
items.summary: For a unit vector \(\vec{n}\) in a Euclidean space \(V\) and an exponent \(p > 1\), the Clifford--Mandelbrot set is generated by \(\vec{x} \mapsto (\vec{x} \diamond \vec{n})^p \diamond \vec{n} + \vec{c}\), where \(\diamond\) is the geometric product. items.title: HERACLES for fast and accurate likelihood-based reconstruction of massive lineages
items.summary: CRISPR-based lineage recording technologies can trace the ancestry of hundreds of thousands of cells, yet reconstructing accurate phylogenies at this scale remains computationally challenging. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Persistent self-improvement enables language-model agents to adapt from experience, but its update process competes with inference for limited device memory, energy, and thermal headroom. items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers.
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison. We show that spectral distinguishability alone bounds the number of labels by the quality factor, M≤Q=2πντ coh . items.title: Hierarchical semantic fusion in hyperbolic space for next POI recommendation.
items.summary: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation aims to suggest POIs that users are likely to visit next based on their recent check-ins. Recent studies suggest that POI-POI transitions and user-POI interactions exhibit hierarchical patterns that can be modeled in hyperbolic space, whose exponential volume growth enables compact and expressive representations. items.title: Unraveling the Ultrafast Photodynamics of Molecular Photoswitches in β-Adrenergic Receptors by First-Principles Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations.
items.summary: Understanding how protein environments regulate the photodynamics of chromophores is a central task in quantum biology and remains a major challenge. This challenge is particularly significant for G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are natively nonphotochromic but can be optically controlled via synthetic photoswitchable ligands. Such artificial photoreceptors are new and important because they not only enable the photocontrol of signaling processes beyond those regulated by rhodopsins but also deepen our fundamental understanding of quantum effects in light-protein interactions.
